title: Lemon Meringue Pie
description:
A classic tart with buttery pastry, tangy lemon filling, and light fluffy meringue topping.

The Meringue is belived to have been invented by a Swiss pastry-cook called Gasparini in 1720. It quickly becaome a favourite of the French court and Marie-Antoinette was apparently so fond of it that she used to make it with her own regal bands!

method.instruction: Lightly grease a 24 cm flan tin.
Sift flour and icing sugar into a bowl. Rub in butter. Add yolk and enough water to bind ingredients.
Form dough into a ball, knead gently on a lightly floured surface until smooth. Cover and refrigerate 30 minutes.
Roll dough to line prepared tin. Trim edges. Place tin on oven tray, line with paper and fill with rice or dried beans.
Bake in moderate oven 10 minutes. Remove paper and beans, bake further 10 minutes until lightly browned. Cool to room temperature.
Combine cornflour and sugar in a pan. Gradually stir in lemon juice and water until smooth.
Cook over heat until mixture boils and thickens (should be very thick).
Reduce heat, quickly stir in lemon rind, yolks, and butter. Stir until butter melts. Cover and cool to room temperature.
Spread filling into cooled pastry case.
Beat egg whites in a small bowl with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add sugar, beating until dissolved and mixture is thick and glossy.
Spread meringue over lemon filling and bake in moderate oven about 5 minutes or until lightly browned.

notes.title: Technique
notes.content: Can be made a day ahead
